Subject: Post-call recap: retrieval & grounding qualification for Cortexa

Hi Alicia —

Great conversation today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up experiments: 

Call summary (high level)
- Primary goal: reduce customer support deflection time by surfacing fully grounded answers from Cortexa docs.
- Success metric: user-facing precision / attribution — Cortexa prioritizes precision over recall.
- Data scope: product docs + FAQs + policy excerpts (~1.2M tokens).

Redwood's recommended starting evaluation plan (short):
1) Models to try (baseline → progressive): Llama-3-8B q4 (fast), Mistral-Instruct-7B trimmed, and Orca-13B-med for a higher-precision run.
2) Retriever config: dense vectors (FAISS IVF-PQ) for initial offline run; chunk size 800 tokens with 128-token overlap; store per-doc metadata (source, section id, last_updated).
3) Candidate retrieval/top_k: pull top 50 by vector similarity (cosine) → rerank top 10 with a cross-encoder for precision.
4) Reranker options: Sentence-BERT bi-encoder for cheap prefiltering + deepset/cross-encoder for final top-10 ranking.
5) Grounding metrics to measure: source attribution rate, hallucination manual spot-check %, exact-match on labeled QA pairs, answer precision on a held-out customer question set. Target thresholds we suggest: precision >= 0.88 on closed QA, < 5% hallucination on sampling.
6) Prompt sets & evaluation: We'll seed with your existing FAQ examples (please send), and run the Redwood eval harness with the prompt variations in sheet attached.

Attachments: Cortexa_eval_plan_v1.xlsx (contains experiment matrix, suggested checkpoints, and evaluation script commands).

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
- Alicia: share export of the FAQ/support examples and one sample customer transcript (by Thu 11/26) — Alicia: ok?
- Redwood (Ben): confirm vector store recommendation and provide exact infra cost estimate (by Mon 11/29).
- Redwood (Soojin/Laura): schedule a 2-week retrieval sprint (plan attached) to deliver baseline runs and quality report.

If that aligns I'll schedule the sprint kickoff for next week and Ben will scope infra.

Thanks again — looking forward to prototyping.

Best,
Soojin

Adding some technical baseline recommendations and a short checklist for the experiments — pulled from the eval playbook.

Retrieval/store recommendations
- Vector store: FAISS IVF-PQ for initial offline experiments (cheap + fast iteration). If Cortexa wants production durability and replication we recommend Milvus or RedisVector via managed fleet.
- Chunking: 800 token windows with 128 token overlap worked well for product docs; set metadata tags for section and source_url.
- Similarity metric: cosine on L2-normalized embeddings.
- Indexing: rebuild nightly during sprint; incremental updates for production.

Retriever/reranker flow (concrete numbers)
- Retriever top_k = 50 (vector store)
- Prefilter: cheap bi-encoder top200 -> cross-encoder rerank top10
- Reranker: cross-encoder checkpoint (sentence-transformers/ms-marco-bertsmall-xx) or a small fine-tuned cross-encoder on your labeled pairs (recommended for higher precision).

Evaluation thresholds & metrics (suggested)
- Closed QA precision >= 0.88 (target)
- Attribution rate (answer cites a source URL in the top-3 results) >= 0.92
- Hallucination rate (manual sample) <= 0.03
- Latency: median inference + rerank < 400ms for Llama-3-8B q4; Orca-13B-med target 450ms median (may require reserved capacity).

Notes on measuring hallucination: we will instrument the eval harness to compute "attribution present" boolean and then sample 1% of answers for manual review (labelled). We can automate a first-pass mismatch detector (answer contains claims not supported by top-5 sources) to prioritize samples.

Infra cost estimate: I'll produce a sprint estimate (GPU hours, vector-store ops) by Monday 11/29 and paste the cost options into the HubSpot deal record.

Link: internal eval notebook + baseline embedding script -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3CortexaEval (read-only link attached).
